text: SURAT: A labourer from Madhya Pradesh was arrested on Saturday evening for the alleged raping and brutal murder of a five-year-old girl living in his neighbourhood in Hazira on April 30. text: NEW DELHI: Tensions escalated at Saket District Court on Saturday as a group of lawyers staged a protest against the Delhi Police over the registration of an FIR against advocates accused of assaulting a police sub-inspector. The Saket Bar Association has called for a strike and barred police personnel from entering the court premises. The protest follows an incident on Thursday, where a sub-inspector alleged that he was manhandled and had his uniform torn by a group of lawyers inside the court complex. The officer had gone to court for a hearing in connection with an ongoing case and later made a PCR call around 2.53 pm, claiming he was assaulted outside court number 508. In response to the FIR filed by the police, the Saket Court Bar Association on Friday issued a notice announcing that its members would abstain from work in protest. Security has since been tightened around the court, with senior police officials deployed to assess the situation. Saket Court Secretary Anil Basoya said, "We don't want strikes, but we are doing this because we are facing injustice... Police has registered a false FIR against lawyers and we are protesting... " Basoya further added that the assault continued inside the court complex. "The police never conduct any investigation on lawyers' complaints... If they fulfil our demand, we will stop the strike; otherwise, this will continue... We will not allow the policemen to enter the court premises or work here," he said. Speaking to PTI, Basoya reiterated the charge of police inaction. "In any matter where a lawyer is the victim, the police refuse to register FIR. Senior officers also don't help, and we then have to approach the court. If the police act against lawyers, then we will also stand against them." The Delhi Police have confirmed that an FIR has been registered and a probe is underway to identify the individuals involved.

text: NEW DELHI: The shooting on the Saket Court complex on Friday again underlined the security loopholes in the city legal complexes despite the tall claims made about heightened security arrangements following the gunning down of gangster Jitender Gogi in a courtroom in Rohini in September 2021. That same year, a DRDO scientist had managed to explode an IED inside a courtroom intending to eliminate a feuding neighbour. Soon after the shootout at Rohini, the security at the seven district courts had been entrusted to Delhi Police's security unit and the central paramilitary force (CPMF) instead of the local police. Several measures were enforced, including allowing only vehicles with stickers or identity cards into the court complexes. Visitors and lawyers at Saket told TOI that it was easy for anyone dressed in black like a lawyer to enter the premises even with firearms and explosives. Dhir Singh Kasana, advocate and former secretary of the bar association, said the main problem was the misuse of parking stickers on car windshields. "Several people gain entry through the old stickers," he claimed. "We have also found that lawyers give stickers that are strictly meant for court officials to their clients." Kasana suggested one sticker for all district courts renewable every year. TOI had highlighted in an earlier report how cars in the city illegally used stickers with 'Judge' or 'Advocate' printed on them. On Friday, when TOI visited the court, the complex had turned into a fortress teeming with policemen and security personnel. Some officers claimed they regularly stopped the advocates for inspections, but the latter refused to be frisked on one pretext or another. "Such a breach of security is a great concern for the lawyers," said Atul Anand. "Some new safety measures had been adopted after the incident in Rohini and in other courts, but a lot still needed to be done. If safety protocols were in place, how did today's shooting take place? Anybody could have been targeted by a shooter." Another lawyer, Ankur Mishra, said that at the time of the firing, there were several lawyers at the spot. "It was peak court hour time. This was definitely a big security lapse," said Mishra. Advocate Masood Khan said that anyone in a lawyer's garb could gain entry to the complex, representing a major loophole. "I have requested the lawyers to cooperate with security personnel during checking," claimed Khan. "If proper security checks had been done, then the person who brought in the pistol might have been caught." While Khan added that proper identity cards and digital car stickers for lawyers was imperative, Vinod Sharma, president, Saket Courts Bar Association, insisted that several measures had been taken to enhance security on the complex.
